title: Charles VI to Count Leopold Viktorin Windischgrätz, 1720-22 (DECODE R5021-R5024), the Emperor's private key R5018

steps.what: Fetched DECODE R5017-R5024 images and record pages; the letter records point to keys R5017 and R5018.
Mírka 2012 found: describes the private key and the Reichshofrat nomenclator, prints no decryption; web search found none.
Transcribed R5018 (24-letter grid of numbers and signs, ~300 codes, nulls).
Nos. 2, 3, 6 read with R5018 letter by letter; drifting copyist signs settled by the surrounding numbered letters.
All 35 passages read as German fitting the clear context and the 1720-22 diplomacy (Alberoni's fall, Beretti Landi marriage proposal).

Entry split from windischgraetz1720 under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): Nos. 2, 3, 6 are in the private key R5018, not the Chancellery key R5017 of No. 1. Fraction measured on these three: 192/192.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): Nos. 2, 3 and 6 linked to dec_R5018_letters.md, which gives each cipher passage's numbers and signs with its decryption; key_file key5018.md

Verification 5 (plain bar, 23 Oct 2026): German (explicit-hole bar): passages in their clear context explicit 1.0 for Nos. 2, 3, 6. Rescored with research/reading_audit/v2_score.py; all entries keep read; reading_review notes record both scores.

outcome.method_basis: The DECODE letter records point to the Emperor's private key R5018, which Mirka (2012) had described; the project transcribed it and applied it directly to Nos. 2, 3 and 6, settling the copyist's drifting signs from the surrounding numbered letters.
outcome.fraction_read_source: dec_R5018_letters.md: 192 cipher tokens of Nos. 2, 3, 6 (37 + 88 + 67); signs marked ? but read in context counted read.
outcome.notes: The key survives and was applied directly; no cryptanalysis. Nos. 4, 5 and 7 of the register are not on DECODE and have no document entry. The clear text is only summarised around the cipher passages. Split on 14 Oct 2026 from windischgraetz1720.

texts.label: No. 2, Vienna, 13 Apr 1720 (R5021 autograph, R5022 copy)
texts.summary: Charles VI to Windischgrätz: whether [Spain] and Orleans will in the end come to terms with one another again, and how one could free oneself entirely from the burden of the Barrier.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (plain bar, VERIFY5_BRIEF): German, not English: explicit-hole bar. The cipher passages of No. 2 in dec_R5018_letters.md put into their quoted clear context (research/reading_audit/v5b_w18.py): plain 1.0 (3/3), explicit 1.0. Keeps read.

texts.label: No. 3, Vienna, 24 Jul 1720 (R5023 copy)
texts.summary: Beretti Landi, the Spanish envoy at The Hague, proposed in his court's name a marriage between one of the Emperor's children and Anjou's sons; Charles will stay on good terms with that court, but 'both are so small' that nothing is to be made known yet, an early trace of the Austro-Spanish marriage scheme of 1725.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (plain bar, VERIFY5_BRIEF): German, not English: explicit-hole bar. The cipher passages of No. 3 in dec_R5018_letters.md put into their quoted clear context (research/reading_audit/v5b_w18.py): plain 1.0 (4/4), explicit 1.0. Keeps read.

texts.label: No. 6, Vienna, 11 Apr 1722 (R5024 copy)
texts.summary: To Windischgrätz as plenipotentiary at the Congress of Cambrai, on his talks with Beretti about a Spanish marriage: Beretti is 'embittered against me and Austria', but it is not bad to make use of him and show him every consideration.
